newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour's Cook doubts UK can stay out of EMU.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour's Cook doubts UK can stay out of EMU.

text.p: Robin Cook, foreign affairs spokesman of Britain's opposition Labour party, said on Thursday he doubted Britain could stay out of a European single currency in the medium term if the single currency proved a success.

Cook told a meeting of the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) that he saw a 75 percent chance of monetary union proceeding but said a question mark remained over whether it would start on time in 1999.
"If the single currency proceeds, I very much doubt in the medium term whether it's possible for Britain to stay out," Cook said.

If Britain were to stay out of a single currency, sterling would become more vulnerable to speculation and foreign investors might show a preference for investing in the core area of the European Union, rather than in Britain, Cook said.
He said that meant Britain would have some freedom in deciding whether to join EMU in the first wave but added "if it succeeds it will not really be an option for Britain to stay outside".
He repeated Labour's position that it would make a hard-headed economic assessment if in government of whether it was in Britain's interest to sign up to EMU.
Cook said Labour saw attractions in a single currency and believed it would be perverse to stay out of EMU if Labour judged it would increase the nation's strength and prosperity.
By the same token he said it would be perverse to sign up for a single currency just as a token of attachment to Europe if it was judged it would harm Britain's strength and prosperity.

If EMU does go ahead, Labour believes there would be a need to strengthen ECOFIN, the EU's council of finance ministers, to provide a political counter-balance to the powerful European central bank in framing macro-economic policy.
